sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: A $40 fee plus $15 per hour totals $115. Write the equation.

steps: Fee is constant; hourly rate multiplies h.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: The formula A = -5bh + 2 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $14 each and item B costs $4 each. You may spend at most $330 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 165 litres and is filling at 3 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 177 litres?
A model gives the number of buses needed as 4.3. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Report 4.3, because the model is exact.
The model must be wrong, because the answer is not a whole number.
Round up to 5; a fractional bus is not viable and rounding down leaves people behind.
Round down to 4, because 4.3 is closer to 4.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $20 call-out fee plus $23 per hour. A job cost $365 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: The formula A = -3bh − 4 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $5 each and item B costs $5 each. You may spend at most $90 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
